source: UNDRO Sudan Drought/Refugees Jan 1985 Situation Reports 1-11 (ReliefWeb archive)
processing_notes: Source states: '10. HEALTH OPERATIONS: SEVERE GASTROENTERITIS OUTBREAKS CONTINUE TO BE REPORTED IN NUMEROUS AREAS INCLUDING KHARTOUM, EL OBEID, NYALA, PORT SUDAN AND NOW MALAKAL IN UPPER NILE AREA OF THE SOUTH. Interpretation: 'severe (acute) gastroenteritis' (SAGE) was the Sudanese Government's official label for the 1985 cholera epidemic, which WHO recorded as cholera (Sudan 1985: 4,457 cases, 239 deaths, notified only from eastern refugee camps); UNDRO Situation Report No. 9 (18 Sep 1985) places the epidemic in Malakal (Upper Nile, southern region) by mid-September 1985 - the only evidence found of cholera in southern Sudan between May 1980 and 1994. Not laboratory-documented for Malakal, no count -> presence at confidence 0.5. TL approximate ('NOW' in the 18 Sep report). Agent 4 batch 5.' - cholera confirmed present; no case count available.
